text:
Here is the test suite in Gherkin (BDD DSL) notation:

```gherkin
Feature: System Scalability and Usability

  Scenario: System can handle 4.0 Million Consultation requests
    Given a 3-year-old database with 4.0 Million Consultation requests
    When the system is queried for consultation data
    Then the system responds with the correct data within a reasonable time

  Scenario: System can handle up to 250,000 unique Patients
    Given a database with 250,000 unique Patients
    When the system is queried for patient data
    Then the system responds with the correct data for all patients

  Scenario: System supports up to 5 specialities
    Given a system with 5 specialities
    When a user selects a speciality
    Then the system displays the relevant data for the selected speciality

  Scenario: System is designed for future growth
    Given a system with a scalable architecture
    When the system is subjected to increased load
    Then the system responds with the correct data without errors

  Scenario: System can run on a mobile platform (Android)
    Given a mobile device with Android operating system
    When the system is installed on the mobile device
    Then the system runs correctly on the mobile device

  Scenario: User interfaces are designed for adaptive response
    Given a user interface with adaptive design
    When the user interacts with the system
    Then the system responds with the correct data and layout

  Scenario: System is designed for usability
    Given a system with user-friendly interface
    When a user interacts with the system
    Then the system responds with the correct data and is easy to use

  Scenario Outline: System handles edge cases
    Given a system with <number> unique Patients and <number> specialities
    When the system is queried for data
    Then the system responds with the correct data

    Examples:
      | number | number |
      | 249,999 | 4      |
      | 250,000 | 5      |
      | 1       | 1      |

  Scenario Outline: System handles invalid input
    Given a system with invalid input <input>
    When the system is queried for data
    Then the system responds with an error message

    Examples:
      | input      |
      | invalid     |
      | null        |
      | empty string |
```
